fixtures.resource_owner_rule: Create only via the UI in this session; capture each POST response ID immediately in the owned ledger. Delete only those exact IDs via UI first, with exact-ID API DELETE fallback and GET 404 verification.
fixtures.test_content_policy: Use deterministic non-executed bash marker text and synthetic non-sensitive defaults/environment values. Never put real credentials in secret-typed parameter fields; record API allowlisted metadata and hashes only.

case_plan.actions: Open Scripts list; search unique fixture name and a guaranteed no-match term; verify row fields; open View, hide and restore one hideable column, then reload and check stored visibility. Observe pagination only if live dataset naturally exceeds one page.
case_plan.oracle: GET /api/scripts count and owned Script row; visible table header/cell values; search hit/no-result UI; column visibility before/after reload and `scripts` localStorage view setting.
case_plan.remaining_or_limit: No extra Scripts may be created for page-size coverage. If live count is below page size, pagination/empty-list dimensions remain PARTIAL; no broad pagination PASS.

case_plan.actions: Use list New link. Type a unique name on new form then Cancel; verify return and zero POST. Later edit only the owned original, make an unsaved name change, then Cancel.
case_plan.oracle: Route `/scripts/new` to `/scripts`; network has no POST; `/api/audit?q=<unique-name>` remains zero. For edit Cancel, GET owned Script and `/revisions` remain unchanged and audit query count/actions do not change. Verify list edit link opens the exact owned editor.
case_plan.remaining_or_limit: Keep unrelated Task-to-Script route evidence separate; do not infer untested return controls.

case_plan.actions: Create the owned Script through the UI with synthetic name/description/content, shell interpreter, `/tmp` working directory, `nobody` run user, timeout 0 (UI min boundary) and enabled state. Verify default/selected field values through save and reopen; toggle enabled/disabled through the list action and restore enabled.
case_plan.oracle: POST-created ID immediately ledgered; GET same ID matches saved fields/revision, including whether timeout 0 round-trips; later edit to 17 checks a typical positive value; list status and subsequent GET confirm enable/disable changes. Compare known-body SHA-256, not raw API body.
case_plan.remaining_or_limit: No Task/Run means cwd/runUser execution remains untested in this batch; keep that dimension PARTIAL. If timeout 0 is rejected or normalized, record exact observed response/readback rather than assuming acceptance.

case_plan.actions: On the new form add each supported parameter type (`string`, `number`, `bool`, `secret`) with known synthetic defaults; save original, reopen, inspect API/UI values, remove selected/all parameters, save again and verify persistence.
case_plan.oracle: GET same owned ID parameter type/name/default allowlist and revision; reopened UI row values/removal; secret default is synthetic only and evidence stores equality/hash, never a credential.
case_plan.remaining_or_limit: Do not run a Script or create a Task to test parameter consumption.

case_plan.actions: Add a synthetic env key, overwrite same key, add a second key; save. Reopen, overwrite the first and delete the second; save and reopen again.
case_plan.oracle: GET same Script environment key/value hashes after each save; UI row shows one current value per key, deleted key absent; no values are secrets.
case_plan.remaining_or_limit: No Task/Run means Agent environment consumption is outside this batch.

case_plan.actions: Create the original Script by the visible Save button, capture the UI POST response ID before assertions, then use UI list/search/open and GET same ID.
case_plan.oracle: Same UI-created ID exists in list and GET with revision 1; server SHA-256 equals local SHA-256 of the known synthetic content; UI success and matching row are visible.
case_plan.remaining_or_limit: Do not substitute API-created fixtures or another ID for this oracle.

case_plan.prior_state: PARTIAL; prior evidence says edit reached revision 2, UI history content expansion remains
case_plan.actions: After clone assertions, edit the original's content/metadata/environment once and Save. Reopen original, expand revision history entries through their actual summary controls.
case_plan.oracle: GET original revision increments exactly +1; `/api/scripts/:id/revisions` returns expected revisions and content hashes; UI expanded `<details>` shows both known body versions, confirmed by safe equality/SHA.
case_plan.remaining_or_limit: Do not treat history section presence without expansion/content comparison as PASS.

case_plan.actions: From the original's actual list row Actions menu choose Clone; immediately ledger the POST response ID. Verify copied row/detail, then edit only the clone once and compare the original unchanged.
case_plan.oracle: Clone has distinct ID, revision 1 at creation, `(copy)` name, and matching original content/parameters/environment; after clone edit, original GET/revision/SHA remains unchanged while clone revision increments.
case_plan.remaining_or_limit: Delete both owned IDs exactly in finally; preserve their audit/revision history according to existing retention policy.

test_interaction.tool: agent-browser CLI using fresh `snapshot -i -u` refs for each UI action; no large single-flow runner.
test_interaction.origin: repair target :18080 through exact owned loopback forward :38181 only
test_interaction.login: Dedicated API login with credentials only in wrapper memory; never print or persist token/password.
test_interaction.audit_oracle: Read-only GET /api/audit?q=<owned unique name or ID>; retain only count and safe action/resource metadata.
test_interaction.cleanup: Dedicated logout -> old token /api/me 401; close browser; exact SSH PID/startticks/argv guard; listener count 0.
